_doc: Per-locale SEO head terms and the field overrides that target them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, SEPARATE FROM src/content/i18n/<locale>.json:
A translation bundle is REGENERATED wholesale by `npm run i18n:merge <loc>`.
Anything hand-tuned inside it is destroyed the next time a locale is
re-translated or a page is added. Head terms are not translations — they are
keyword decisions backed by Semrush data (SEO-BRIEF 8.2) — so they live here
and are applied AFTER the translation merge, where no merge run can clobber
`headTerms` is also the expectation the guard test reads: every money page
(home/feature/type archetypes) in a live locale must carry its locale's head
term in the title. That is what stops a new locale silently shipping titles
that render the ENGLISH page's intent instead of targeting native demand.
Matching is accent- and hyphen-insensitive (see test/seo-head-terms.test.mjs).
German 'QR-Code-Generator' and Spanish 'códigos' therefore satisfy the terms
'qr code generator' and 'codigos' without anyone having to write incorrect
German or misspelled Spanish to chase a query string.
Money pages only. Articles and industry hubs deliberately do NOT carry the
generator head term — they take question/comparison and vertical intent and
link down. See the cannibalization table in the article spec.

de.note: English form dominates. 'kostenlos' 9,900 owns the free modifier; 'qr-code erstellen' 1,600 carries verb intent and is served by the meta.

es.note: PLURAL beats singular (1,600 vs 1,300). The unaccented spelling in SEO-BRIEF 8.2 is a query-typing artifact, not a copy instruction — Google folds diacritics for Spanish, so titles keep correct 'códigos'. es DB; pull MX separately for LatAm.

pt-br.note: Second-largest remaining market. The English-style 'QR code' beats 'código QR' — never write 'gerador de código QR' in a money-page title, it loses the term. '...gratis' 1,000 carries the free modifier. Localize examples to Brazil (PIX rather than generic card payment).

id.note: The ENGLISH form dominates Indonesian search — this term is copy, not a translation, and stays English inside Indonesian titles and H1s. Native forms are secondaries for meta and body only: 'buat kode qr' 2,400, 'pembuat kode qr' 720. A title that says 'pembuat kode QR' instead of 'QR code generator' loses the head term.
